chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Be afraid of the ideas of believers, because Allāh, the Sublime, has put truth on their tongues.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be afraid of the ideas of believers in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) instructs believers to be cautious of the conjectures or opinions of other believers, as God has placed truth upon their tongues. This highlights the spiritual insight and reliability of the faithful in matters of perception and judgment. In Shia tradition, this hadith is often interpreted to mean that the 'truth' on their tongues refers to their intuitive discernment (fitrah) and reliable testimony, serving as a safeguard against hasty judgment while reminding us that even their guesses are rooted in divine proximity.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 309. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Be afraid of the ideas of believers, because Allāh, the Sublime, has put truth on their tongues.
